newsitem.title: UK: Netanyahu arrives in Britain at start of Europe tour.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu arrives in Britain at start of Europe tour.

text.p: Hardline Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu arrived in Britain at the start of a European tour on Tuesday and compared Palestinian militants to IRA guerrillas.

Since taking office in June, Netanyahu has made two visits to Israel's main ally, the United States, to garner support for his right-wing government and for his tough attitude to peace with the Palestinians. Now he has turned to Europe.

"These visits are a natural continuation of the contacts we have had since our government was formed," Netanyahu said on arrival in London. "Also, from a bilateral standpoint, Israel is quickly turning into a European and Western economy, in the full sense of the words."
He said the Jewish state wanted to "deepen these ties," referring to economic relations.

But there were other points of cooperation, said Netanyahu, who was headed straight to a meeting with British Prime Minister John Major. "In Britain, for example, I think you will find a certain understanding."
Britain and Israel stood almost alone in giving unreserved support to Washington in its response to Baghdad's incursion into Kurdish-held territory in northern Iraq.
Netanyahu compared the struggle for peace in Northern Ireland with Israel's relationship with Palestinians.

"Britain is also dealing now with a wave of terrorism and I hope to raise with Mr Major the import of our approach, which calls first for halting terrorism and action to ensure security as guarantees of peace," he said.
"Therefore, as someone who has dealt with terrorism, he is surely familiar with the demand for mutuality in respecting agreements."
Israel says it will move ahead with the Middle East peace process only if the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) succeeds in cracking down on attacks by Islamic militants.

Netanyahu's Labour predecessor, Shimon Peres, agreed a peace deal with PLO leader Yasser Arafat, granting Palestinians a measure of self-rule, freezing Israeli settlements on Arab land and withdrawing Israeli forces from some self-rule areas.

The IRA is fighting to end British rule in Northern Ireland, and mainland security forces scored a major victory against Europe's most persistent guerrillas by seizing tonnes of explosive and killing a guerrilla suspect on Monday.
Britain demands that the IRA restore a ceasefire before they can join all-party talks on the future of Northern Ireland.
"I think that these things will be spelled out in more detail and depth in my meeting with Major," Netanyahu said.
Netanyahu will also meet opposition Labour Party leader Tony Blair and former Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher.
He flies to Paris on Wednesday for talks with President Jacques Chirac and Prime Minister Alain Juppe before travelling to Bonn on Thursday to meet Chancellor Helmut Kohl.
